name: Trouble in Pairs
oracle_text:
If an opponent would begin an extra turn, that player skips that turn instead.
Whenever an opponent attacks you with two or more creatures, draws their second card each turn, or casts their second spell each turn, you draw a card.
blocked_sentences: Whenever an opponent attacks you with two or more creatures, draws their second card each turn, or casts their second spell each turn, you draw a card.

needs.what: a selector key that keeps only creatures attacking a PLAYER (not a planeswalker that player controls), e.g. {"binding": "attackers", "attacking_player": true} or an `attacking_planeswalker: false` filter reading `combat.attacking_planeswalker`, so the creatures_attack_player trigger's condition can count "two or more creatures attacking you" rather than "attacking you and/or planeswalkers you control"
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `creatures_attack_player` with `defending: you` fires with `attackers` = every creature whose defending player is you, and combat.py deliberately folds planeswalker attacks into that set ("attacking the walker is attacking its controller, and one event covers both halves"). Mangara, the Diplomat can count that binding because its text says "you and/or planeswalkers you control"; Trouble in Pairs says only "attacks you", so one creature at you plus one at your planeswalker would wrongly draw a card. The `attacking` selector key is a bare boolean with no notion of whom, and nothing in selector_keys or value_keys reads `combat.attacking_planeswalker`. Everything else on the card is expressible: the first sentence is static `skip_extra_turn` with `affects_player: opponent`, the draw/spell-cast clauses are `draw` and `spell_cast` triggers with `controller: opponent, nth: 2`, and the pool already splits one printed "X or Y" trigger sentence into several triggered abilities sharing the same `text` (Mirkwood Bats, Grave Titan, Stitcher's Supplier).
